key_insight: A workflow-integrated LLM system can automatically generate daily radiation oncology summaries and trial matches, and clinicians reported high adoption and favorable usability after 1 month.
clinical_relevance: This suggests AI can reduce routine information-gathering burden in radiation oncology while helping clinicians identify potentially relevant clinical trials during standard care.
method: Cross-sectional anonymous clinician survey after 1 month of deployment.
Daily physician-specific email summaries generated by RadOnc-GPT from EHR data, schedules, and trial-matching outputs.
Mixed-methods early evaluation focused on usability, satisfaction, usefulness, workflow impact, time savings, and future use.
evidence_signal: In 55 respondents, most used the tool daily or several times per week, mean ratings were positive across domains, and overall Cronbach's alpha was 0.97.
watch_item: Findings are early, self-reported, and from a single deployment, so broader effectiveness, safety, and generalizability still need confirmation.
paper_title: The Daily Dose: Workflow-Integrated Large Language Model Automation for Clinical Summarization and Trial Identification in Radiation Oncology
